meta.title: Docs
meta.description: Get started with MCPEmails in minutes. Quick-start guide, tool reference, and example responses for Gmail, Outlook, and IMAP agents.

hero.lead: Connect any email account, paste one URL into an OAuth-capable MCP client and authorize. Clients without OAuth use an API key instead. Full tool reference and connection guide below.

quickstart.heading: Up and running in minutes.
quickstart.sub: No SDK required. MCPEmails speaks standard MCP over HTTP, so it drops into any MCP-compatible agent.

signup.label: Sign up & connect an inbox
signup.heading: Create your account and connect Gmail
signup.body: Sign up at mcpemails.com, then go to Dashboard → Inboxes → Connect Inbox. Pick Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, or any IMAP inbox, then complete the OAuth flow or paste an app password. Your inbox is ready in under a minute.

apikey.label: Create an API key
apikey.heading: Generate a bearer token for your agent
apikey.body: In Dashboard → API Keys, click "Create key". Name it, select the scopes your agent needs — from read:email and send:email through manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email — and copy the key. It is shown only once.

addclient.label: Add MCPEmails to your agent
addclient.heading: Paste the MCP endpoint into your client
addclient.body: Pick the tab for your client below. MCP clients with OAuth 2.0 support (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) just paste the URL and authorize, no API key needed. Clients without OAuth, plus scripted access, use the API key from step 02.

firstcall.label: Make your first call
firstcall.heading: Ask your agent to check your inbox
firstcall.body: No copy-pasting inbox UUIDs. Your agent calls list_inboxes first to discover every connected inbox and its UUID, then you ask: "Check my inbox and summarise the last 5 unread messages."

endpoint.heading: One URL, standard MCP.
endpoint.sub: All traffic goes to a single Streamable HTTP endpoint. Authenticate with a bearer token from your dashboard.
endpoint.bodyMethods: Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request body. Supported methods: initialize, tools/list, tools/call.
endpoint.pollingBody: MCPEmails is request/response only: every result comes from a tool call your agent makes. There are no webhooks, push notifications, or server-initiated events — an incoming email never triggers an agent call on its own. To react to new mail, have your agent poll on a schedule, e.g. call list_messages with unread_only: true at whatever interval your workflow needs (mind the rate limits above).

oauth.heading: Zero-config for OAuth-capable clients.
oauth.sub: MCP clients that support OAuth 2.0 (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) connect automatically via authorization code + PKCE. No API key, no config file. Paste the URL and click Connect.
oauth.step1: Step 1: Go to claude.ai → Customize → Connectors → Add connector
oauth.step3: Step 3: Click Connect. MCPEmails opens an authorization screen
oauth.step4: Step 4: Sign in with your mcpemails account and approve access
oauth.stepDone: Done: Every tool your approved scopes allow is live. claude.ai refreshes tokens automatically
oauth.howTitle: How it works under the hood
oauth.howP1: claude.ai registers itself via RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, so you never pre-register a client ID.
oauth.howP2: Authorization uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636), so no client secret is ever transmitted.
oauth.howP3: Tokens are scoped to exactly the permissions you approve — from read:email and send:email through manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email.
oauth.noOauthNote: Using a client without OAuth support? Create an API key in Dashboard → API Keys and pass it as a bearer token. API key and OAuth connections use the same MCP endpoint and the same tool catalogue.

tools.heading: 33 tools. Every email operation your agent needs.
tools.sub: Start with list_inboxes to discover available inboxes and their UUIDs — every other tool takes an inbox_id returned by that call. Tools are grouped by the scope that unlocks them; tools/list only returns the tools your key (or OAuth token) is scoped for. Click "Show example" to see a full request and response.

read.title: Read & search
read.desc: Discover inboxes and folders, list and read messages, and run provider-native searches. Read-only — never changes anything.

send.title: Send & message state
send.desc: Send, reply, and forward, plus non-destructive state changes: mark read/unread, flag/unflag, archive, and bulk flag. Sends are irreversible.

folders.title: Folders & organization
folders.desc: Create, rename, and delete folders (labels on Gmail), and move or copy messages — one at a time, in bulk, or straight from a search.

delete.title: Delete
delete.desc: Trash or permanently expunge messages — one at a time, in bulk, or from a search. Every delete requires confirm: true.

drafts.title: Drafts
drafts.desc: List, create, update, and send drafts stored in the provider's Drafts folder.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.desc: Search a contact list built automatically from the From, To, and Reply-To headers seen in your mail. No manual setup.

schedule.title: Scheduled send
schedule.desc: Queue an email for a future time, list pending scheduled sends, and cancel them before they go out.

tools.noParams: No parameters. Call with an empty arguments object:

list_inboxes.title: List Inboxes
list_inboxes.desc: Returns every inbox the current API key or OAuth token can access. Call this first to discover inbox_id values, so you never copy-paste UUIDs from the dashboard. Each result includes the email address, provider, optional service brand (icloud/yahoo/zoho/yandex/generic/fastmail), and a capabilities object describing which features that inbox supports.

list_messages.title: List Messages
list_messages.desc: List email summaries from a connected inbox, newest first. Supports pagination, folder selection, and unread filtering.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to list. Call list_inboxes first to discover available inbox IDs.
params.limit: Max results to return. Default 20, max 100.
params.folder: Folder to list. Default "INBOX". Other values: "SENT", "DRAFTS", "TRASH".
params.unread_only: Return only unread messages. Default false.

read_email.title: Read Email
read_email.desc: Fetch the full content of a single email by ID, including plain-text body, optional sanitized HTML, and optional attachment data.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the email. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.
params.include_html: Include sanitized HTML body. Default false.
params.include_attachments: Include base64 attachment data. Default false.
params.mark_as_read: Mark message as read after fetching. Default false.

search_emails.title: Search Emails
search_emails.desc: Search an inbox using provider-native query syntax. Gmail supports Gmail search operators; Outlook uses $search; Fastmail and IMAP inboxes use text search.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.query: Search query. For Gmail: "from:alice@example.com after:2026/01/01". For Outlook: natural-language or KQL queries.
params.include_folders: Restrict search to these folder names. Default: search all folders.

send_email.title: Send Email
send_email.desc: Send a new email from a connected inbox. Supports plain text, optional HTML body, CC/BCC, and file attachments (up to 10 MB total).

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.subject: Email subject line. Max 998 characters.
params.html_body: HTML version of the body (multipart/alternative). Caller is responsible for safe HTML.
params.attachments: File attachments. Each item: '{' filename, mime_type, data (base64) '}'. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

reply_to_email.title: Reply to Email
reply_to_email.desc: Send a reply to an existing email. Threading headers (In-Reply-To, References) are set automatically. Supports reply-all and attachments.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that contains the original message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the email being replied to.
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the reply.
params.reply_all: Reply to all original recipients (To + Cc). Default false.
params.attachments: File attachments. Same schema as send_email. Max 20 items.

mark_read.title: Mark Email as Read
mark_read.desc: Mark a single email message as read. Non-destructive — it only changes the read flag, never deletes or moves the message. Works across every provider.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.

list_folders.title: List Folders
list_folders.desc: List every folder (or label, on Gmail) in an inbox. Each entry has the provider-native folder ID, display name, type (folder vs label), and message counts. Use the IDs as the folder argument for list_messages and as the source/destination for move and copy.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose folders to list. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.

forward_email.title: Forward Email
forward_email.desc: Forward an existing message to new recipients. Your optional note is prepended above a standard forwarded-message header block and the original body. Set include_attachments to re-attach the original files. The subject is prefixed with 'Fwd:' if needed. Irreversible.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that holds the original message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the email to forward, from list_messages or search_emails.
params.body: Optional plain-text note to prepend above the forwarded message.
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the note (multipart/alternative).
params.include_attachments: Re-attach the original message's attachments. Files over the 10 MB budget are omitted. Default false.

mark_unread.title: Mark Email as Unread
mark_unread.desc: Mark a single email message as unread. Non-destructive — only the read flag changes. Works across every provider.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.

flag_email.title: Flag Email
flag_email.desc: Flag (star / mark for follow-up) a single message. Non-destructive. Maps to the provider's native star or flag — Gmail STARRED label, IMAP \Flagged, Outlook flag, Fastmail $flagged keyword.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.

unflag_email.title: Unflag Email
unflag_email.desc: Remove the flag (star / follow-up mark) from a single message. Non-destructive.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.

archive_email.title: Archive Email
archive_email.desc: Move a message out of the Inbox to the archive. Non-destructive — the message is preserved, not deleted. On Gmail this removes the INBOX label; on IMAP/Outlook/Fastmail it moves to the Archive mailbox.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages or search_emails.

bulk_flag.title: Bulk Flag
bulk_flag.desc: Apply one read/unread/flag/unflag action to up to 500 messages in a single call. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus a per-message result list.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to update. Max 500 per call.
params.action: Action to apply to all messages: "read", "unread", "flag", or "unflag".

create_folder.title: Create Folder
create_folder.desc: Create a new folder (or label, on Gmail) in an inbox. Returns the provider-native folder/label ID and display name.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to create the folder/label in. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.name: Name of the new folder or label. 1–255 characters.

rename_folder.title: Rename Folder
rename_folder.desc: Rename an existing folder or label. Call list_folders first to obtain the folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the folder/label.

delete_folder.title: Delete Folder
delete_folder.desc: Permanently delete a folder (or label, on Gmail). Irreversible — messages inside may be lost depending on the provider. Requires confirm: true. Call list_folders first to obtain the folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the folder/label.
params.confirm: Must be true to confirm this destructive operation.

move_email.title: Move Email
move_email.desc: Move a message to a different folder. On Gmail this adds the destination label and removes INBOX (Gmail has no separate folders). Call list_folders to obtain the destination_folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the message.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages, read_email, or search_emails.
params.destination_folder_id: Provider-native folder/label ID of the destination, from list_folders. For IMAP this is the mailbox name; for Gmail the label ID; for Outlook/Fastmail the opaque folder ID.

copy_email.title: Copy Email
copy_email.desc: Copy a message to another folder, leaving the original in place. Not supported on Gmail (the Gmail API has no native copy) — use move_email there instead. Call list_folders to obtain the destination_folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the message.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages, read_email, or search_emails.
params.destination_folder_id: Provider-native folder ID of the destination, from list_folders.

bulk_move.title: Bulk Move
bulk_move.desc: Move up to 500 messages to a destination folder in one call. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus per-message results. Call list_folders to obtain the destination_folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to move. Max 500 per call.
params.destination_folder_id: Provider-native folder/label ID of the destination, from list_folders.

search_and_move.title: Search and Move
search_and_move.desc: Run a search and move every match to a destination folder in one server-side operation — avoids stale message IDs. Capped at 500 matches per call. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus per-message results.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search and operate on.
params.query: Search query, in the inbox's native syntax (Gmail operators, Outlook KQL, or IMAP search).
params.destination_folder_id: Provider-native folder/label ID of the destination, from list_folders.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names. Default: all folders.
params.limit: Maximum number of matches to move. Default 500, max 500.

delete_email.title: Delete Email
delete_email.desc: Delete a single message. By default it moves to the provider's Trash (safer). Set permanent: true to hard-delete (bypasses Trash; may be irreversible). Requires confirm: true. Permanent expunge is available on IMAP and Fastmail; Gmail and Outlook support trash only.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the message.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_messages, read_email, or search_emails.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.
params.confirm: Must be true to confirm this destructive operation.

bulk_delete.title: Bulk Delete
bulk_delete.desc: Delete up to 500 messages in one call. Defaults to Trash; set permanent: true for a hard delete. Requires confirm: true. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus per-message results.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to delete. Max 500 per call.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.
params.confirm: Must be true to confirm this destructive operation.

search_and_delete.title: Search and Delete
search_and_delete.desc: Run a search and delete every match in one server-side operation — avoids stale message IDs. Capped at 500 matches per call. Defaults to Trash; set permanent: true for a hard delete. Requires confirm: true.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search and operate on.
params.query: Search query, in the inbox's native syntax (Gmail operators, Outlook KQL, or IMAP search).
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete matches (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names. Default: all folders.
params.limit: Maximum number of matches to delete. Default 500, max 500.
params.confirm: Must be true to confirm this destructive operation.

list_drafts.title: List Drafts
list_drafts.desc: Return drafts saved in the inbox's Drafts folder. Each result includes the draft_id, subject, recipients, and created timestamp. Use the draft_id with update_draft or send_draft.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose drafts to list.
params.limit: Maximum number of drafts to return. Default 20, max 50.

create_draft.title: Create Draft
create_draft.desc: Save a new draft in the inbox's Drafts folder without sending it. Returns a draft_id for update_draft or send_draft. Subject and body are required; recipients are optional (drafts may be incomplete).

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to save the draft in.
params.subject: Draft subject line.

update_draft.title: Update Draft
update_draft.desc: Replace the content of an existing draft. All supplied fields overwrite the stored draft. Call list_drafts to obtain draft_id values.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the draft.
params.draft_id: Provider draft ID from create_draft or list_drafts.
params.subject: Updated subject line.

send_draft.title: Send Draft
send_draft.desc: Send a previously saved draft. The draft is removed from the Drafts folder after sending. Irreversible.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that contains the draft.
params.draft_id: Provider draft ID from create_draft or list_drafts.

search_contacts.title: Search Contacts
search_contacts.desc: Search the derived contact list by name or email. Contacts are built automatically from the headers seen during read, search, and send — no manual setup. Returns matches sorted by most-recently-contacted, each with display name, email, message count, and last-contacted timestamp.

params.query: Name or email fragment, matched case-insensitively against display name and address. At least 1 character.
params.inbox_id: Optional. Restrict results to contacts seen from one inbox. Omit to search across every inbox the key can access.
params.limit: Maximum number of contacts to return. Default 20, max 50.

get_contact.title: Get Contact
get_contact.desc: Retrieve the full contact record for one email address within an inbox: display name, address, cumulative message count, and last-seen timestamp. Call search_contacts first to discover known addresses.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox associated with the contact.
params.email_address: The email address to look up. Matched case-insensitively.

schedule_send.title: Schedule Send
schedule_send.desc: Queue an email to be sent at a future time. Recipients and body are validated immediately; if validation fails it is not queued. The dispatcher runs every minute, so actual delivery may be up to 60 seconds after send_at. Use list_scheduled and cancel_scheduled to manage pending sends.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from.
params.subject: Email subject line. Max 998 characters.
params.send_at: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone at which to send. Must be in the future, e.g. "2026-06-02T09:00:00Z".
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the body.
params.attachments: File attachments. Same schema as send_email. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

list_scheduled.title: List Scheduled Sends
list_scheduled.desc: List pending scheduled sends for the workspace (status pending or sending), earliest first. Optionally filter by inbox. Use cancel_scheduled to cancel one before it dispatches.

params.inbox_id: Optional. Restrict results to scheduled sends for one inbox.
params.limit: Maximum number of results. Default 20, max 100.

cancel_scheduled.title: Cancel Scheduled Send
cancel_scheduled.desc: Cancel a pending scheduled send so the dispatcher skips it. Only sends still in 'pending' state can be cancelled — once 'sending', 'sent', or 'error' they cannot. Use list_scheduled to find the scheduled_send_id.

params.scheduled_send_id: UUID of the scheduled send to cancel.

errors.heading: Error codes & retry guidance.
errors.sub: Auth, scope, and rate limit failures return a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code. Tool execution failures (inbox not found, provider error, etc.) return a normal result with isError: true and a human-readable message in content[0].text.

rows.auth: Missing, malformed, revoked, or expired API key. Also returned when the API key lacks the required scope for the called tool.
rows.method: Unknown JSON-RPC method (e.g. calling a method other than initialize, tools/list, tools/call)
rows.param: Unknown tool name, or missing / invalid parameter in tools/call
rows.rate: Per-key rate limit or plan daily quota exceeded. Check data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" vs "quota_exceeded". Check data.retry_after (seconds) before retrying.
rows.tool: Tool executed but encountered an error (inbox not found, message not found, provider auth failure, invalid recipient, attachment too large, provider 5xx). The error description is in content[0].text.

rateLimits.heading: Rate limits & quotas.
rateLimits.perKeyBody: Enforced per API key regardless of plan. When exceeded, the server returns error code -32029 with data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" and a data.retry_after field (seconds). Respect that value before retrying.
rateLimits.planHeading: Free 60 / min · Solo 300 / min · Team 1,000 / min
rateLimits.planBody: Usage is unlimited; this is a per-workspace fair-use burst limit (aggregated across all your API keys). When exceeded, calls return data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" with data.window: "per_minute" and a data.retry_after countdown (seconds). Upgrade your plan for a higher ceiling.
rateLimits.retryHeading: Always honour retry_after; never retry sends blindly
rateLimits.retryBody: For rate_limit_exceeded errors, wait data.retry_after seconds before retrying. Use exponential backoff for provider_error. Do not auto-retry send_email on provider_error, since the message may have already been accepted by the provider.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Start on the Free plan: unlimited, no card required. Upgrade to Solo or Team for higher burst limits and team features.

meta.title: Provider Support
meta.description: See which email providers MCPEmails supports and which features are available per provider: Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP.

hero.heading: What works, per provider.
hero.lead: MCPEmails connects Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, and any IMAP inbox (iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, generic). Not every provider exposes the same APIs — this table shows exactly what each one supports today.

legend.imapNote: Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP all connect over the same IMAP/SMTP transport (Fastmail and iCloud use an app-specific password) and share an identical feature set, including IMAP search syntax. The columns are shown separately for clarity.

notes.gmail: Gmail — folders vs labels: Gmail uses a flat label system rather than hierarchical folders. "Move" is implemented as label add/remove. Native copy is not available via the Gmail REST API.
notes.permanentDelete: Permanent delete: Gmail and Outlook move to Trash when you delete — permanent expunge is not exposed by their APIs. IMAP providers (Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, Generic) support both trash and hard expunge.
notes.contacts: Native contacts API: Gmail uses the Google People API; Outlook uses Microsoft Graph /contacts. Fastmail CardDAV and IMAP-based contacts are out of scope for v0.1.
notes.contacts_db: Contact search (DB-synced): All providers automatically populate a contacts table from From, To, and Reply-To headers seen during read, search, and send operations. Use search_contacts and get_contact to query it.
notes.scheduling: Scheduling: Supported for all providers via a server-side scheduled_sends queue. Use schedule_send, list_scheduled, and cancel_scheduled. Delivery uses each provider's existing send path — no provider-native scheduling API is required.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Free plan: unlimited connections, no card required.
